paper.title: Instance-Dependent Regret Bounds for Nonstochastic Linear Partial Monitoring

unmapped: Linear partial monitoring: action a has feature x_a in R^d (loss x_a^T l_t) and known observation matrix M_a; learner observes M_{A_t}^T l_t
Loss space is a convex compact set containing a centered L2 ball B_2(r)
Learner knows the feature map and observation matrices (game structure)
Observability class (locally / globally observable) is a game property
settings.definition_quote: Before the game starts, the adversary secretly chooses a sequence of loss vectors $(\loss_t)_{t \in [T]}$, where $\loss_t \in \Loss$. Then, at every round $t \in [T]$, the learner: i) selects (possibly at random) an action $A_t \in \mathcal{A}\,$; ii) observes the signal $\signal_t\coloneqq M_{A_t}^\top \loss_t \in \mathbb{R}^{n(A_t)}$, which, in general, is distinct from the incurred (but unobserved) loss $\feat{A_t}^\top\loss_t\in\mathbb{R}$.

symbols.Lambda_star: Lambda*_eta, optimal value of the per-round EXO program (sup over q)
symbols.eps_tol: sub-optimality tolerance of the per-round optimization

source.label: prop: regret UB with Lambda star
source.quote: Under global observability, \Cref{alg:main} satisfies $ R_T \leq \frac{\log k}{\eta} + \eta \Lambda^*_\eta T + (2\delta + \eta \varepsilon) T $.

results.notes: Regret is expectation over learner's randomness vs best fixed action against oblivious sequence. Holds for any eta; horizon labelled known since tuning of eta uses T.

symbols.C_loc: max over losses of inf over local weightings lambda of beta_lambda^2 * min{rank(M), |supp(lambda)|}
symbols.rank_M: rank of stacked observation matrix M

source.label: cor:simpler-lambda-bound-local
source.quote: In locally observable games, it holds that $\Lambda_\eta^* \leq \max_{\loss \in \Loss} \inf_{\bm{\lambda} \in \Mloc_{\loss}} 8 L^2 \beta_{\bm{\lambda}}^2 \min\{\rank(\bm{M}),|\supp(\bm{\lambda})|\} + 2 L ( 1+ \beta_{\glo}^2) \min\{\rank(\bm{M}),w^*\}$ provided $\frac{1}{\eta} \geq 2 L ( 1+ \beta_{\glo}^2) \min\{\rank(\bm{M}),w^*\}$

results.notes: Bound on the EXO optimization value Lambda*_eta, not on regret directly; combined with Proposition 1 it gives regret. Simplification in text: Lambda*_eta <= 12 L^2 beta_loc^2 d when L, beta_loc >= 1.

symbols.beta_glo: global alignment constant (sum of block norms)
symbols.rank_M: rank of stacked observation matrix M

tuning: eta small enough as in regime

source.label: cor:simpler-lambda-bound-global
source.quote: In globally observable games, it holds that $\Lambda^*_{\eta} \leq 4 \sqrt{{1}/{\eta}} L \min \{ (1+\beta_{\glo}) \sqrt{\min\{\rank(\bm{M}), w^*\}}, (1+\beta_{2,\glo}) \sqrt{u^*} \}$ provided that ...

results.notes: Bound on Lambda*_eta; regret follows via Proposition 1.

symbols.alpha_loc: constant alpha with Lambda*_eta <= alpha (from local theorem, e.g. 12 L^2 beta_loc^2 d)

source.quote: Assuming $\delta$ and $\varepsilon$ are sufficiently small, setting $\eta=\min \{1/B,\sqrt{\log k/(\alpha T)} \}$ yields via \Cref{prop: regret UB with Lambda star} that $R_T$ is $\cO ( \sqrt{\alpha T \log k})$.

results.notes: Informal corollary in text. Instantiations: full info O(sqrt(T log k)); strongly observable graphs O(sqrt(alpha(G) T log k)); linear bandits and linear dueling bandits O(sqrt(d T log k)). Adaptive variant (Alg. 2) attains the same order.

symbols.alpha_glo: constant alpha with Lambda*_eta <= alpha/sqrt(eta) (from global theorem)

source.quote: setting $\eta=\min \{1/B,(\log k/(\alpha T))^{2/3} \}$ yields via \Cref{prop: regret UB with Lambda star} that $R_T$ is $\cO ( (\alpha T)^{2/3}(\log k)^{1/3})$.

results.notes: Informal corollary. Instantiations: weakly observable graphs O((delta(G) log k)^{1/3} T^{2/3}) with delta(G) total domination number; composite graph feedback O((k log k)^{1/3}(beta_2glo T)^{2/3}).

conditions: bandits with ill-conditioned observers: d=k, x_a=e_a, M_a=(1-eps)1_k/k + eps e_a

source.quote: Since $e_a - e_b = 1/\varepsilon (M_a-M_b)$, we have that $\beta_{\mathrm{loc}} \leq 2/\varepsilon$. Thus, the regret bound is of order $1/\varepsilon\sqrt{k T\log k}$.

results.notes: Instantiation in text; matched up to logs by Theorem 4.

conditions: at least two non-duplicate Pareto optimal actions

source.label: prop:lowerbounds
source.quote: Assume that the game has at least two non-duplicate Pareto optimal actions, and that $\cB_2(r) \subseteq \Loss$ for some $r>0$. Then, the minimax regret $R^*_T$ is $\tilde{\Omega}(\sqrt{T})$ if the game is locally observable, $\tilde{\Omega}(T^{2/3})$ if it is globally but not locally observable, and ${\Omega}(T)$ otherwise.

results.notes: Minimax lower bound; proved as Theorem 2 in appendix with explicit form r||v|| sqrt(T)/(32 sqrt(60 log T)) - sqrt(2) alpha* r for T large.

conditions: game is globally but not locally observable

source.label: prop:lowerbounds
source.quote: ... $\tilde{\Omega}(T^{2/3})$ if it is globally but not locally observable ...

conditions: bandits with ill-conditioned observers: d=k, x_a=e_a, M_a=(1-eps)1_k/k + eps e_a

source.quote: In the bandit game with ill-conditioned observers, it holds that $R_T^*$ is $\tilde{\Omega}(\nicefrac{1}{\epsilon}\sqrt{kT})$.

results.notes: Proof gives explicit sqrt(kT)/(64 eps sqrt(2 log(16T))).
